Correct sentence:__ *He was not **__able to adapt himself __****__to__** the new environment of the hostel.*

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

NFTs are

P. digital collectables that exist on

Q. and are better known for recently

R. taking the art world by storm

S. online ledgers known as blockchains
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e. "**PSQR**." 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the abovementioned paragraph, there is a chronological sequence of the sentences.
 
• **Sentence P** is the first part of the sentence as it begins with the noun 'NFTs' and introduces the topic of the sentence, namely NFTs, which are digital collectibles.
 
• **Sentence S** is the second part of the sentence as it begins with the preposition 'on' and specifies where NFTs exist and how they are created and stored. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence as it ended with 'exist on.'
 
• The only option that shows such an arrangement is **Option 1**.
 
• **Sentence Q** is the third part of the sentence as it begins with the conjunction 'and' and provides further information about NFTs and why they are significant.
 
• **Sentence R** is the last part of the sentence as it begins with the verb 'taking' and highlights the recent popularity of NFTs in the art world. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
• Therefore, the complete sentence reads:** "NFTs are digital collectables that exist on online ledgers known as blockchains and are better known for recently taking the art world by storm."**

**The correct order is: **__

NFTs are

P. digital collectables that exist on

S. online ledgers known as blockchains

Q. and are better known for recently

R. taking the art world by storm

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.**

I __told__ Rahu __on__ wait __for__ two hours __at__ the bus stop.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 4) i.e. 'on.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'on.'
 
• In the erroneous part, the use of the preposition** 'on'** is wrong as the verb** 'wait'** is in the base form.
 
• We need to use** 'to'** before the base form of the verb.
 
• The word **'to'** in the erroneous segment will be acting as part of the '**to-infinitive'. **The to-infinitive is formed as** 'to + base form of the verb'.**
 
• The **to-infinitive **is used in many sentence constructions, often expressing the purpose of something or someone's opinion about something.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *She told Anil **to eat **the burger.*
 
 
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'to' in place of 'on' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct sentence:__* **I told Rahu __**to**__ wait for two hours at the bus stop.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

“Meena, will you assist me to pack our belongings?” asked her mother.

options.text: Meena's mother asked her whether she will assist her to pack their belongings.
Meena's mother asked her whether if she would assist her to pack their belongings
Meena's mother asked her whether she would assist her to pack their belongings.
Meena's mother asked her whether she can assist her to pack their belongings.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) 'Meena's mother asked her whether she would assist her to pack their belongings.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is an interrogative sentence in Direct Speech. As per the given directions, we have to change it into Indirect Speech.
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
• The conjunction 'whether' will be added and comma and inverted commas will be removed.
 
• In the Indirect speech 'asked' will not be changed because the reporting verb has no object.
 
• The subject **'her mother'** will be changed into **'Meena's mother.'**
 
• Also a reflexive pronoun **'her'** will be added to address the question in the indirect speech.
 
• The indirect speech will begin like 'Meena's mother asked her whether.'
 
• Now we have to change the reported speech.
 
• Here the pronoun 'you' will be changed into 'she' and 'me' will be changed into 'her.'
 
• Also, 'our' will be changed into 'their'
 
• The future tense 'will' will be changed to the past tense 'would'.
 
• Here, 'will you assist me to pack our belongings?' is in an interrogative sentence and will be changed into an assertive sentence i.e., 'she would assist her to pack their belongings.'
 
• Finally, the indirect speech is 'Meena's mother asked her whether she would assist her to pack their belongings.'
 
• So, the correct answer is option 3.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *Meena's mother asked her whether she would assist her to pack their belongings.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Huda lived in / the southern part / off Germany.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 1) i.e. 'off Germany.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'off Germany.'
 
• In the given sentence, the correct preposition to use is **"of"** instead of **"off."**
 
• **"Of"** is a preposition that indicates the relationship between two things, such as possession, origin, or cause.
 
• **For example:**
 
 
• **​***Children have the qualities **of **their parents.*
 
 
 
• Whereas*, ​*"off" is also a preposition that indicates separation or distance between two things.
 
• **For example:**
 
 
• *Her car swerved and plunged **off** the cliff.*
 
 
 
• The given sentence indicates that Huda lived in a particular region within the country Germany.
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'of' in place of 'off' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct sentence:__* **Huda lived in the southern part **__of Germany__.***

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

Our machine is shipped to ten different countries.

options.text: We shipped our machine to ten different countries.
We are shipping our machine to ten different countries.
Someone ship our machine on ten different countries.
We ship our machine to ten different countries.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. 'We ship our machine to ten different countries.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **passive voice**. We have to change the sentence into the **active form. **
 
• The given sentence is written in 'present indefinite tense' form. 
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• Passive Voice: Object + is/are + V3 + by + Subject
 
• Active Voice: Subject + V1 + Object.
 
 
 
• Let’s see another example:
 
 
• Passive voice: The ambulance is called by us.
 
• Active voice: We call the ambulance.
 
 
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'our machine' and the subject of the given sentence is silent which is 'us' as the correct form of the sentence also can be 'Our machine is shipped** ****to ten different countries** by us.'
 
• So, in the active voice, the position of ‘object’ and ‘subject’ will be interchanged.
 
• Also here, the silent subject 'us' will be changed into 'we.'
 
• The V3 'is shipped' will be changed into V1 'ship.'
 
• The remaining part will not be changed.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *We ship our machine to ten different countries.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The citizens have chosen that man as their leader.

options.text: That man had been chosen by the citizens as their leader.
That man has been chosen by the citizens as their leader.
That man is chosen by the citizens as their leader.
That man was chosen by the citizens as their leader.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e. 'That man has been chosen by the citizens as their leader.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice**. We have to change the sentence into** passive form**. 
 
• The given sentence is written in 'present perfect tense.'
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• Active Voice: Subject + have/has + V3 + Object.
 
• Passive Voice: Object + have/has + been + V3 + by (preposition) + Subject.
 
 
 
• Let’s see another example:
 
 
• Active voice: I have eaten the muskmelon.
 
• Passive voice: The muskmelon has been eaten by me. 
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'The citizens' and the object of the given sentence is 'that man'. 
 
• So, in the passive voice, the position of ‘subject’ and ‘object’ will be interchanged. 
 
• Also here, 'have chosen' will be changed into 'has been chosen'.
 
• The remaining part will be the same.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *That man has been chosen by the citizens as their leader.*

questions.question:
**Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.**

Neither the teachers (or the principal likes the new budget) cuts.

options.text: either the principal likes the new budget
or the principal like the new budget
nor the principal like the new budget
nor the principal likes the new budget

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4), i.e., 'nor the principal likes the new budget.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in Part (or the principal likes the new budget) of the sentence.
 
• As per instructions, the remaining portion of the sentence is correct.
 
• According to the rules of correlative conjunctions, ‘either ...... or’, ‘neither ..... nor’, ‘both ..... and’, ‘not only ...... but also’, ‘though .... yet’, ‘whether...or’ are used in pairs.
 
• The given sentence begins with **'Neither' **so** 'nor' **will be used with it.
 
• **Option 3,** "nor the principal like the new budget," has **incorrect subject-verb agreement.**
 
• If two subjects are joined by **"neither...nor", **the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. In this case, the subject nearest to the verb is '**principal**' which is singular. Thus, a singular helping verb is needed i.e. '**likes**'.
 
• **Option 4,** "nor the principal likes the new budget," is absolutely correct.
 
• Therefore, in the erroneous part, the use of 'or' in the sentence should be replaced with 'nor' to make it grammatically correct.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Correct sentence:__ *Neither the teachers __**nor the principal likes the new budget**__ cuts.*

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P. I had my own crib in the bedroom next to our parent’s room.

Q. Annie awoke hungry at 2:30 a.m. each morning.

R. When Annie would cry out, I would climb out of my crib and come running into our parent’s room to check on her.

S. For the first few months, Annie slept in a crib by our parents’ bed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. "SPQR." 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the abovementioned paragraph, there is a chronological sequence of the sentences.
 
• Sentence S is the first sentence as it begins with the phrase 'For the first few months'. This sentence establishes the setting of the story, indicating where Annie slept during the initial period i.e., in a crib by the parents’ bed. This sets the context for the rest of the paragraph.
 
• Sentence P is the second sentence as it begins with the noun 'I' and explains that the speaker had her/his own crib in the bedroom next to their parents' room. This further develops the setting and explains where the speaker slept in relation to Annie. Thus, it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
 
• The only option that shows such an arrangement is Option 4.
 
• Sentence Q is the third sentence as it begins with the noun 'Annie' and introduces a new idea - that Annie would wake up hungry at 2:30 a.m. each morning. This creates a sense of urgency and sets up the problem that the speaker needs to solve.
 
• Sentence R is the last sentence which explains how the speaker responded to Annie's cries by climbing out of their own crib and running into their parents' room to check on her. This provides a resolution to the problem set up in the previous sentence and shows how the speaker took care of their younger sibling. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

The correct order is:__ 

**S.** For the first few months, Annie slept in a crib by our parents’ bed.

**P.** I had my own crib in the bedroom next to our parent’s room.

**Q.** Annie awoke hungry at 2:30 a.m. each morning.

**R.** When Annie would cry out, I would climb out of my crib and come running into our parent’s room to check on her.
